posts.body_html: Both those photos are from Stone County, MS in the DeSoto National Forest. These populations see regular burns from the Parks Service. The flowering photo was taken at sunrise. I was with Jim Miller who was shooting video of the last large native stands of these plants. We went all across the panhandle in 4 days shooting film. What a great adventure.

posts.body_html: Fantastic shots, Brooks, and thanks for sharing that info!  We are very lucky that these sites are being well maintained and are in fact thriving.  I've been talking to other people in the Carolinas, and the same can't be said for many of the populations in the mountains, which are being overgrown by native vegetation.  The land has been changed so drastically that it now requires humans to intervene for their very survival.
